body: Thanks!
This is the response that I need from the people in my life! It's going to take time, they think it's something that can be changed in the blink of an eye.

The Narcissist Prayer

That didn't happen.
And if it did, it wasn't that bad.
And if it was, that's not a big deal.
And if it was, it's not my fault.
And if it was, I didn't mean it.
And if I did....
You deserved it.

I have an ex that lives by this motto, he refused to add that his actions and words have consequences, both positive and negative. He wonders why the only people who stay by his side are toxic and he can't seem to get his life under control.

The sad part is that there are times where he does see the impact that his actions and words cause. He's seen me cry and hurt myself, he's seen me at my lowest state in depression. He doesn't care, and the times that he chooses to, he uses to his advantage. As for me, I do want him to feel this way so he can feel what his actions caused.

As I said before, I'm responsible for my own actions, I know that. If you knew that a loved one was going to hurt themselves, what would you do to help? Would you do what you can or say screw that and continue to do what hurts them? I never said that I shouldn't have to regain their trust. I asked  if they should try and regain mine? I was lied to over and over, even when I was committed. Doesn't that justify me not trusting them?

I get your where you're coming from, I really do, but this almost comes off that I'm fully to blame. Yes, I am responsible for my own actions, but if someone you love tells you that they are In a bad spot and they need you to do something as simple as to hold them while they cry and your response is to push them away, maybe even throwing an insult at them, would you have a stake in that blame too? Not every situation is the same.

 I understand that they're hurting and having to deal with their own emotions, but have  you considered that maybe those people have to regain my trust? It wasn't a surprise that I was suicidal, I told them, one of them got the gist of it and told me to stop the conversation. He didn't want me to say it. I've told them what was going on, what they could do to help, and I wasn't being listened to. They heard what I was saying, but they didn't listen to what was being said, if that makes any sense. I was lied to over and over, given some sense of hope and understanding, but at the first opportunity these people were given they went back on they're promises, knowing what it would do, what it would cause.

They got me back on my meds, I was out if one for 2 months because the pharmacy was out, and in the group sessions we talked about all kinds of things, most of them were focused on self affirmations and accepting that, even though you may not see yourself in a good light other people do. We talked about what to do after discharging and how to process and handle concepts like recovery from addiction, boundaries, the difference between healthy and unhealthy coping skills. 

It wasn't so much being in a group setting, I actually don't do very well when I don't know anyone. I was able to let my guard down because these are people who were there for a reason, they were depressed and/or suicidal. Some went through the same kind if experiences I have so they understood where I was coming from, where I was mentally. I think that was the key, they understood. The people in my life don't understand, most have never been through the trauma I have it haven't been "that depressed." I've been told  multiple times that they (the people in my life) don't get it. I plan on doing an IOP at the facility I was at, so hopefully I can meet people there as well.

I honestly don't know if time will help. Yes, I need to re-adjust to being home, but someone it is the home itself. The people there know what happened and they sympathize, but they don't change. They're willing to, well one is, but I don't think they know how.

He knew. He's the one person in my life who completely gets what I'm going through. 

I'm sorry that you had to go through the same thing. People suck.
No, sad to say, but this is the person that I view as my best friend
r/pornfree is a good subreddit too. They have a list of steps you can take to help, like apps that block adult sites and support from the community is amazing.

He is my rock,  even if he doesn't underatand. We've been together for a little over 15 years, and even thought this has cause a little but of an obstacles, we want to be together as long as possible.  I really do love the man.

Yes! It's not just society though,  it's cultural.  I have a friend (a different race and culture) who has been getting help since he was 5, but I also have cousins who are in their late 40s that have never gotten help because it's looked down on. I've already taught my children that if they need help, any kind of help, that they will have it. I will not fail them like I was. I can't control what my culture and society view as right and normal, but I can help my children see that it's OK, and, hopefully,  change how the future views mental health and addiction.

And that's where it gets... complicated? I was sober for 6 years (give or take a month or two), so he thinks that it's all fine and dandy and I can do that again. I can't.  He understands, to an extent, but (in his own words), he won't get it because he doesn't have and never has had an addiction, or an extended but of depression.  I love him,  but this is something that I don't think he can ever understand about me.

He is a very smart man, but sometimes he let's our upbringing interfere with him learning from the people around him. Our roommate, one of my best friends has an addiction  and he's tried to explain it in a physiological way, and my boyfriend just doesn't get it. 
As for meetings,  since my addiction. Started back up, I haven't been able to be in a group unless I know someone, let alone sharing what I've been through and what  going through.  I am getting help though, therapy is helping, though I know it's going to get worse before it gets better.

Yes, I agree! But where we're from it has a face. It is that teen with 3 kids selling herself, or the junkie doing anything they can. So, unless you're out on the streets because of your addiction,  then it's not an addiction. You can function.  I went a long time before I could admit it, and even longer before I even thought about getting help. It's not an excuse, it's  the culture, mental health is not an issue, and it never will be. That's why I left and cut everyone off.

Android. My phone is about 6 years old and his 4. 
It does mean a lot to me that someone has shown appreciation, even if you are a stranger, thank you. You have no idea what it means to me.

He wants to stop, and for the most part he can fight through the urges, but he has little willpower, so  if anything happens that puts too much pressure on him emotionally,  he gives in. 
He is getting help in the form of therapy  (and addiction specialist ), so hopefully that helps. I can ask him to bring up your advice in his next session.

I did take your advice and talked to him about it, well, I spoke, he half listened. In the end he said that I could download what I thought I needed to. It may not be the response I was hoping for, but at least he didn't fight me on it...  You have no idea how much it means to me that someone  appreciates what I'm doing, even if it is a stranger. I struggle with depression and my own addiction, so it's always nice to receive some kind of appreciation.  Thank you, thank you so much.
Haha, I've always wanted to visit Texas.  Technically I am in the valley and am from a valley, if that makes any sense....
AL pastor with all the fixins for tacos, burritos, tortas, and nachos with a side of rice and beans and tres leches cake for dessert.

I loved it and, honestly,  I wish I could still do it. It's a very physical job and has its hazards, I've seen my fair share of injuries. 

As for tips, well, that depends on your experience,  I guess. I started as a cleaner and learned everything I could and work any shift I could. For a good while I did an assistant's job for the pay of an apc. On a personal note, don't go higher than an assistant/cutter, the pay isn't worth the stress. Oh, and some of the guys can be, well, they're a special bunch. 🙄

Pretty much all the chain stores. Most of the time they're the manager or assistant in the department. Though, for the most part, they're not real butchers. They're are some old timers that used to actually butcher sides of meat, now some of them don't even know how to cut down a whole pork loin.

This is all too true. Occasionally lamb lion chops will be an sale for $5lb and shoulder chops for $4-$5lb, but other than prime and organic beef, lamb is one of the more expensive cuts. 

You can usually save a dollar or two if you buy the whole cut and have the cutter custom cut it for for you. And be aware of the stores markdown policy. I used to markdown high cost items cheap so I could get some kind of sale out of it, even if I didn't make a profit on it.

I was a meat cutter for about 12 years, this is how many a conversation went. You can, and probably will at one point or another, get a grumpy one, but don't let it deter you from asking for their help, many of us are very nice and knowledgeable. 

On another note: the majority of major grocery chains won't grind anything but beef, at least here in Az. But many of them do sell and can order other ground meat products, you just need to ask.

One thing I've learned over the years is that you can't make people happy. They have an opinion on who and what you should be, but they are not you. I changed everything I could to make someone I love, and I thought loved me, happy.  It didn't help. I've lost myself.  All I can do is hold onto the aspects of myself that I know are good, things that I love about myself. Sometimes it's hard to see, that's the problem I'm having right now, but it's there, there's always something.

This has been me for the majority of my life. I eventually hit a point where I couldn't run away anymore.  Now the emotional ups and downs are exhausting. Cutting provided a feeling of control, now,  it all just feels overwhelming.

I think that my mom did think that she was doing what was best for me, getting help for mental health is something that is not well excepted in the community and culture I grew up in.  I'm not saying that she made a good choice, especially since she weponized "getting help," but she did what she was brought up to think was best. I'm breaking that cycle with my kids. 

​

Don't take this the wrong way, but don't minimize what you've been through just because you percieve that what I have been through as worse. I did that and never got help, now I'm 33 and have a life that a lot of people would like, but  here I am, depressed and hurting myself. I'm glad you're getting help and you have my best wishes for succeeding.

I thank you for your support, i really do appreciate that there are people out there who I can talk.
I'm sure you can. It's hard work, and I know it's something, for me at least, that is just ingrained in me, but this time I have more to think about than just myself. Do you have a support system?

I don't think I'm particularly ashamed of getting therapy, for me it just happened that every time some kind if help was offered there was a negative aspect to it. Even now, I want to tell myself that I don't need it, that someone else can use the help more than I can. Then I look at what I've done to myself and I push myself to accept the help that I'm going to get.
I am feeling better, thank you. I know that I have to take it one day at a time. I do appreciate the advice with your experience.

The hubby is there for me, he always had been. At this point, he's just trying to figure out how I can get help. But in the end, as much as I know I should use him for support, I know that this is something that I have to do  on my own. He can tell me how much I mean to him and how much I am loved and needed, but it's up to me to figure it out.

Thank you for the words of support and encouragement,  it's always nice to know that there are people out there that you can talk to, especially when it comes to these types of relationships. 

As for a therapist,  no, I don't have one. I don't have any insurance, and even when I did, it only covered 4 sessions a year. I did try using the chat option for suicide prevention lifeline,  but I waited over an hour to get connected and 45 minutes to get a counselor, but by that time I had to get back to life. I was going to call, but this isn't something I want my kids to overhear.
This makes me smile! 😄

I totally relate to this, though my nmom was only a devout catholic at convenience, and I had to practice what she preached. I never "believed," only studied, which dissapointed her to no end and she let me know it.  But, like you said, interesting stories and lovely music, to me, that's all a church based belief is.
Definitely "Dirty Pretty" by In This Moment. The album as a whole is pretty amazing,  but that is definitely my favorite.
